claim: For two thousand years, Chinese statecraft has carried a codified set of thirty-six stratagems.
source: [1] *Thirty-Six Stratagems* (三十六計), traditional; the received text dates to the Ming or late Qing period, with individual stratagems drawn from far older sources including the *Book of Qi* and *Romance of the Three Kingdoms*.

claim: Rather than assault every fortified Japanese garrison in his path, American strategy bypassed the strongest ones, Rabaul and Truk among them, cutting their supply and leaving tens of thousands of defenders to wait on islands the war had already moved past.
source: [2] Pacific island-hopping strategy; the bypassing of Rabaul and Truk, 1943–1944. U.S. Navy operational histories.

claim: The Doolittle Raid on Tokyo in April 1942 did negligible material damage and struck the one target Japan could not afford to leave undefended, pulling carrier strength home in time to be caught short at Midway two months later.
source: [3] Doolittle Raid, April 18, 1942; Battle of Midway, June 4–7, 1942.

claim: The Destroyers-for-Bases deal of September 1940 traded fifty aging warships for ninety-nine-year leases on British bases across the Atlantic, negotiated at the exact moment Britain could least afford to refuse.

Royal Engineers laid miles of dummy pipe crawling south, timed to look complete just when a southern attack would need it, while real armor massed in the north disguised as ordinary supply trucks under painted canvas.
source: [5] Operation Bertram, the deception plan for Second El Alamein, October 1942.

claim: The American 23rd Headquarters Special Troops, the Ghost Army, built entire fake divisions from inflatable tanks and recorded convoy noise, and German reconnaissance filed reports on formations that existed nowhere but on the airwaves.
source: [6] 23rd Headquarters Special Troops, 1944–1945; unit records declassified 1996.

claim: Congress passed the Two-Ocean Navy Act in July 1940 while Britain and Germany bled each other, building the fleet that would decide the Pacific before American forces had fired a shot in either ocean.
source: [7] Two-Ocean Navy Act, Pub. L. 76-757, July 19, 1940.

claim: BGI's NIFTY prenatal test, developed in collaboration with the People's Liberation Army and marketed in more than fifty countries, has collected genetic material from millions of women worldwide under a medical banner, and the samples feed a state-run gene bank whose own privacy policy reserves the right to share data for national security purposes.
source: [8] BGI Group NIFTY test; PLA collaboration documented in published research co-authorship. **Scoped:** the draft gave "over eight million women" and "since 2013"; company statements and press investigation give differing counts and start dates, so the text now states the scale qualitatively. U.S. National Counterintelligence and Security Center public statements on PRC genomic collection.

claim: The Alsos Mission followed advancing Allied armies into Germany with no combat mission at all, scooping up scientists, documents, and equipment behind every division that took new ground, a goat pilfered at every stop no single unit was fighting to claim.
They sent P-38s to intercept his aircraft over Bougainville and killed him directly.

A homeless man's body, dressed as a fictional Royal Marines officer and released off the Spanish coast carrying false invasion plans, sent Germany reinforcing Greece and Sardinia while the real target, Sicily, went ashore three weeks later against a lighter defense.

Britain's Tizard Mission handed America its most advanced radar and jet-engine research in 1940 in exchange for the industrial capacity to build on it at scale, a brick of raw manufacturing power returned as jade in finished weapons within years.
What followed was an occupation, Anglo-Soviet forces controlling the country's government and territory for the war's duration and after, the corridor never closed once it was granted.
source: [13] Operation Countenance, Anglo-Soviet invasion of Iran, August 25 – September 17, 1941.

claim: RAF bombers over Hamburg in July 1943 dropped bundles of foil strips, code-named Window, that returned so many false echoes German radar operators could no longer separate an actual bomber stream from static, and the raid went in nearly unopposed.
source: [14] Operation Gomorrah, July 1943; first operational use of Window (chaff).

claim: American forces learned the doctrine the hard way at Kasserine Pass in February 1943, driven back by Rommel in the United States Army's first major defeat of the war.
source: [16] Battle of Kasserine Pass, February 19–24, 1943; Patton assumed command of II Corps March 6, 1943.

claim: The Double-Cross System let its turned agents pass genuine, verifiable, low-value intelligence back to Berlin precisely so the credibility earned by real losses would be spent on the one deception, Fortitude, that mattered.
source: [17] The Double-Cross System, official history released via the National Archives.
